coverage_note: Selected primary-source checks, not exhaustive weekly monitoring. Event dates can be publication dates or vendor-announced rollout dates; verification is not independent replication. Radar items do not change the registry cutoff or acceptance counts.

assessments.headline: From signal encoding to longitudinal reasoning
assessments.summary: Physiology-aware generation and long personal histories extend representation learning into richer temporal context.
assessments.limit: Preprints; no prospective disease-prediction or clinical-utility validation.

assessments.headline: Action claims need intervention evidence
assessments.summary: Frameworks and controlled trials answer different questions. Judge actions against outcomes and identification assumptions.
assessments.limit: No new intervention result verified in the selected weekly window.

assessments.headline: Useful twins remain disease-specific
assessments.summary: Individual diabetes models couple repeated feedback with adaptation; whole-person causal twins remain an open research agenda.
assessments.limit: Predictive, mechanistic and causal twins are not interchangeable.

assessments.headline: Glasses are becoming a programmable entry point
assessments.summary: Inputs and developer tooling are advancing; delivery status and regional availability need separate tracking.
assessments.limit: Vendor evidence; avatars are not health twins or complete spatial MR.

signals.availability: Rollout announced from September 30; universal availability not independently checked.
signals.title: Meta DAT 1.0: developer preview → supported release
signals.before: A year of developer-preview integrations and developer-mode testing.
signals.after: A supported toolkit connects mobile-app logic to glasses camera, speech, head motion and Neural Band input.
signals.evidence: Meta's developer announcement dates the rollout start to September 30.
signals.limit: WebMCP remains preview; connectors are early access; discovery is coming soon. Not an independent performance test.
signals.implication: A concrete integration surface for future personal-model interfaces, not proof that a twin or full MR system exists.

signals.availability: UK/Canada sales and US online ordering announced; France/Italy/Germany preorders, supply planned October 13. Hologram US early access later this fall.
signals.title: Meta Display: wider sales; face-avatar calls announced
signals.before: The 2025 launch used selected US retail locations.
signals.after: More markets and online ordering; a voice-driven face avatar is announced for hands-free calls.
signals.evidence: Official launch and availability statements, not an independent hands-on assessment.
signals.limit: Preorder is not delivery. The avatar infers expressions from speech; it is not a physiological twin. A HUD is not automatically spatial MR.
signals.implication: Separate the interaction entrance from the underlying body model, and track feature delivery by region.

signals.availability: Research preprint; not accepted into the frozen registry.
signals.title: SOTER: physiology-aware forecasting and imputation
signals.before: General time-series transfer or static physiological representations.
signals.after: Cross-channel dependencies, frequency-informed expert routing and continuous-time decoding.
signals.evidence: Authors evaluate six datasets: best zero-shot RMSE on four, MAE on five, and best imputation at 75% missingness on six.
signals.limit: Preprint and author-run comparisons; hospital waveforms are not all free-living wearables. No prospective clinical benefit.
signals.implication: Track temporal and physiological structure as an enabling method, not a validated disease predictor.

comparison.baseline: Paper's general time-series and physiological-model comparators.
comparison.result: Dataset-specific best scores, not a single universal improvement percentage.
comparison.conditions: Use the paper's matched forecasting/imputation protocols; tasks and metrics differ across datasets.

signals.availability: Research benchmark preprint; not accepted into the frozen registry.
signals.title: WearableQA: longitudinal personal-data reasoning
signals.before: Text-only health QA or directly prompting over long sensor sequences.
signals.after: 4,084 ten-choice questions across 200 people, with up to 500 days of wearable histories and additional health context.
signals.evidence: Table 2: the same GPT-5.4 scores 51.2% with row-wise CoT and 71.3% with fixed-representation agentic Python access.
signals.limit: Tool access and computation change. This is QA accuracy, not a weight upgrade, diagnosis accuracy or clinical benefit.
signals.implication: A testbed for reasoning over personal histories; not an evolving, causally validated individual twin.

comparison.result: Same model, fixed-repr agentic Python access: 71.3% (+20.1 percentage points).
comparison.conditions: Same WearableQA benchmark; different tool access and compute. Do not compare this with disease-prediction metrics.

signals.availability: Published small clinical trial; event date is publication, not trial completion. Not yet cataloged.
signals.title: T2D predictive twin: weekly model updates, daily feedback
signals.before: Self-monitoring and periodic care without model-generated daily feedback.
signals.after: Individual transfer learning, weekly retraining and daily SMS suggestions with nurse-scored safeguards.
signals.evidence: Single-centre randomized substudy: 19 participants, 10 AI and 9 control; three-month intervention after three-month baseline. Weight differed; glucose stayed stable.
signals.limit: Authors describe a predictive twin, not a fully bidirectional, real-time mechanistic twin. Small sample; not proof of glucose improvement.
signals.implication: Inspect which twin properties exist and which outcomes changed before treating personalization as a full twin.

signals.availability: Published conceptual framework, not an empirical trial or deployed system.
signals.title: Causal digital twins: a framework, not a clinical result
signals.before: Predicting a person's trajectory does not identify what changing treatment would do.
signals.after: A framework combines causal models, potential outcomes and sequential policy optimization.
signals.evidence: Peer-reviewed methodological proposal; no new dataset, benchmark or empirical effectiveness test.
signals.limit: Identification assumptions, individual calibration and prospective intervention utility still require evidence.
signals.implication: Use as a technical checklist for the prediction-to-intervention route, not a reported performance breakthrough.

signals.availability: Published randomized trial; event date is publication, not trial completion.
signals.title: AID co-adaptation: a bounded physiological-twin baseline
signals.before: Automated insulin delivery with conventional feedback rather than twin-guided co-adaptation.
signals.after: Individual glucose-insulin models support parameter optimization and personal what-if replay.
signals.evidence: 72 participants, six-month randomized trial. The twin-guided co-adaptation package improved time in range; information feedback alone added no effect.
signals.limit: Type 1 diabetes-specific physiology, not a whole-body twin. A 2025 result must not be presented as this week's news.
signals.implication: A useful intervention-validated reference for judging later twin claims, within its reported population and protocol.
